body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application:

br.br:
1. (Original) A method for overriding autonomous control of a device, the method comprising:controlling a control lever of a device via a first actuator during manual operation mode of the device, wherein the first actuator is coupled to the control lever via a rod;
controlling the control lever of the device via a second actuator during autonomous operation mode of the device, wherein a resettable frangible link couples the second actuator to the control lever via a rod; and
entering the manual operation mode by the rod receiving an applied force via the first actuator causing the resettable frangible link to separate the second actuator from the rod.
2. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the resettable frangible link includes a magnetic coupling having a first half and a second half to couple the second actuator to the control lever via the rod, and the method further comprises:realigning the first half and the second half of the magnetic coupling causing a magnetic attachment of the first half and the second half in order to reattach the second actuator to the rod for reentering the autonomous operation mode of the device.
3. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein controlling the control lever comprising controlling operation of the device using a bell crank movement.
4. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the control lever is a throttle lever, and the device is an engine coupled to the throttle lever, wherein controlling the first actuator or the second actuator controls operation of the engine.
5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the resettable frangible link enables separation of coupling of the second actuator from the control lever at any rotational orientation of the control lever with respect to the device.
6. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the control lever is a throttle lever for an aircraft, the first actuator is a control rod for a pilot to use to control the throttle lever, and the second actuator is another control rod that is controlled by a computing device for autonomous operation.
7. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the first actuator is permanently attached to the control lever via the rod.
8. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the first actuator and the second actuator each have an ability for independent control of the control lever, wherein based on the applied force to the rod by the first actuator, the first actuator overrides the second actuator.
Attorney Docket No. 19-1114-US-DIV
9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the resettable frangible link includes a mechanically frangible control rod to couple the second actuator to the control lever via the rod.
10. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the resettable frangible link comprises:a base for mating with a fitting of the second actuator;
a brace attached to the rod; and
a mechanically frangible control rod having a first end and a second end.
11. (Original) The method of claim 10, wherein each of the first end and the second end of the mechanically frangible control rod is threaded such that the first end attaches to the base and the second end attaches to the brace.
12. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the resettable frangible link includes a magnetic coupling having a first half and a second half to couple the second actuator to the control lever via the rod.
13. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the resettable frangible link comprises:a base for mating with a fitting of the second actuator;
a magnet positioned in the base;
a brace attached to the rod; and
a magnetic pole piece positioned in the brace, wherein the magnet is magnetically connected to the magnetic pole piece.
14. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein the brace includes a threaded portion for attaching to corresponding threads on the rod.
15. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein the magnet is a permanent magnet.
16. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the resettable frangible link includes an electro-magnet, and the method further comprises:controlling a magnetic attraction force of the electro-magnet by a control system coupled to the electro-magnet.
17. (Original) The method of claim 16, further comprising the control system altering the magnetic attraction force based on an operating condition of the device.
18. (Original) The method of claim 16, further comprising detecting, by a sensor, an angle of the resettable frangible link with respect to the second actuator, and wherein the control system alters the magnetic attraction force based on the angle.
19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the resettable frangible link includes a magnetic coupling having a first half and a second half to couple the second actuator to the control lever via the rod, and the first half and the second half of the magnetic coupling are configurable to be realigned causing a magnetic attachment of the first half and the second half in order to reattach the second actuator to the rod for reentering the autonomous operation mode of the enginedevice.
Attorney Docket No. 19-1114-US-DIV
20. (Original) The method of claim 19, wherein the resettable frangible link includes an electro-magnet, and the method further comprises:controlling a magnetic attraction force of the electro-magnet by a control system coupled to the electro-magnet.
